question: Which firms have co-developed several robotic construction processes with partners?

answer.answer:
Firm_060 is the only repeat partner of any weight in this material, named in three of the eight joint-development records, with Firm_061 and Firm_082 next at two each and every other firm appearing once. The partnerships themselves range from two firms up to seven, so "several partners" is common while "several projects with partners" is rare. On the coded side, the organisational route to an integrated design-DFAB process (AT12) splits between early contractor involvement (CO11), drawn on by 14 of the 50 coded cases, and vertical integration (CO10) at 25, the latter pulling towards a single tightly coupled firm rather than the consortium pattern these records show, with a coordinating role (AC4) evidenced in only 8. Note that the census records retrieved here are not linked to the enabler layer in front of me, and that the wording of "firm", "co-developed" and "process" is mine and only loosely matches the record's own terms of manufacturer, distributor and developer.

**Firms appearing in more than one joint-development record**

Firm_060 is the clearest repeat collaborator. It appears in census_RXM6-4, jointly developed with Firm_168, Firm_008, Firm_009 and Firm_064 [1], in census_RXM6-7 with Firm_061 and Firm_079 [2], and in census_RXM6-6 with Firm_061 [3]. The edges refine the roles: in census_RXM6-4, Firm_060 is recorded as a manufacturer alongside Firm_008 and Firm_168, while Firm_009 and Firm_064 are recorded as distributors rather than makers. Both of the later records use steel as the material node.

Firm_061 follows with two records, census_RXM6-7 [2] and census_RXM6-6 [3], in each case partnered with Firm_060, so it is better read as a standing partner of one firm than as an independent hub.

Firm_082 also appears twice, but with two different counterparts: census_RXM8-3 with Firm_072 [4] and census_RXM8-1 with Firm_003 [5]. That makes it the second genuine hub in this set, connecting otherwise unrelated partners.

Every other firm named appears once: the seven-firm partnership behind census_RXM23-5 (Firm_177, Firm_002, Firm_018, Firm_068, Firm_094, Firm_134, Firm_209) [6], the pairing of Firm_097 and Firm_098 on census_RXH8-2 [7], which uses timber, and Firm_027, Firm_028 and Firm_033 on census_RXH5-4 [8], the one record where the graph states the relation as developedBy rather than hasManufacturer. This is a retrieved selection of census records, not the whole census, so a firm absent here may well recur elsewhere.

**The one record tied to a deployed process**

Only census_RXM6-4 is linked to a Process record, as the census record of RP14. What that record gives is the division of labour, Firm_168, Firm_060 and Firm_008 as manufacturers with Firm_009 and Firm_064 distributing, not a description of the task performed or the site. The remaining seven census records stand alone in the material retrieved, so I cannot say what any of these machines did on a project.

**How the coded framework treats this pattern**

Multi-firm development touches three enablers that share a single target, AT12 "Integrated design-DFAB process" (Attribute), drawn on by 19 of the 50 coded cases, which lets them be compared directly. AT12 hasPrecondition CO10 "Vertical integration", on the argument that technically interdependent systems require tighter organisational coupling such as a single firm [9], an edge carried by 14 of the 50 and backed by peer-reviewed evidence; CO10 is the upstream requirement here. CO10 also enablesCapability AT12 as a management approach for digital fabrication adoption [9]. CO11 "Early contractor involvement" enablesCapability AT12, on evidence that BIM and early contractor involvement improve design management and increase adoption [9], carried by 10 of the 50. AC4 "DFAB design coordinator" enablesCapability AT12 through interdisciplinary team integration [9], carried by only 7 of the 50, with AC4 drawn on by 8 of the 50 coded cases [9]. The asymmetry matters: the coordinating actor role that a seven-firm partnership like census_RXM23-5 would seem to need is the thinnest of the three, while the best-evidenced route, vertical integration, runs the opposite way from consortium development.

CO11's own reach extends beyond design integration: it enablesCapability PR2 "Prefabrication/off-site", on the argument that integrating manufacturing and assembly knowledge into design requires the delivering production party to be involved in the early design phase [9], carried by 13 of the 50, and it enablesCapability PR9 "DfMA for DFAB process" as one of the DfMA enablers for offsite work [9], carried by 11 of the 50. Those are CO11's three cited edges in full, so partner involvement in the record is framed almost entirely as a design-phase and off-site matter.

One further enabler is directly relevant and unconnected in the literature: AC8 "DFAB contractor" (Actor) is drawn on by 25 of the 50 coded cases and carries no dependency edges at all [9]. Half the coded record involves a contractor actor, yet nothing in the cited layer links that actor to anything, which is a gap in the literature rather than in the record. This is the general condition of the Actor category, 88% of which carries no cited edge. [9]
